title: outline 0.6 names the command that gives the next Q#
intention: Outline 0.6 carries no hand-kept next Q#: it names cairn outlinecheck --next-qnum, which prints the number the mint would give, and 0.6 carries no Q# marker of its own, so a hand placing a marker never takes a number already given.
why: Measured 2026-11-24: outline 0.6 reads 'which is now 128' while number_open gave Q#128-Q#135 the same day, so a hand reading 0.6 takes a number already given; and 0.6's own by-line spells '[Q#127]', which joined.markers reads as Q#127's marker in 0.6 (the first section it meets), so the joined outline files Q#127 under 0.6 and cairn outlinecheck b03dce633aa8 opened open-4f53f113cd1b on it. The cast's first reading (47 numbers on two records; Q#126/127 with no record) was refuted at build: see measured.
traces_to: Law 9 — a broken spec line on disk is red until fixed; Law 1 — a Q# is the address a settled answer is found by.
how: outline_check's CLI gains --next-qnum, printing next_qnum over the commons; 0.6's 'which is now 128 (... [Q#127] ...)' becomes a pointer at that command, with no count and no bracket; 741d's tooth reads the pointer instead of the count; a new proof holds the three clauses.

clauses.claim: cairn outlinecheck --next-qnum prints outline_check.next_qnum over the commons it is pointed at: 12 over a scratch commons whose records reach Q#11, and next_qnum over the live one
the live outline states no hand-kept next unused number and 0.6 names cairn outlinecheck --next-qnum
joined.markers reads no Q# marker in section 0.6 of the live outline

decisions.text: D1: a new proof cairn/devices/codemother/machines/outline_check/proofs/test_outline_06_names_the_command_that_gives_the_next_q.py, a scratch-commons tooth for clause 1 and live teeth for clauses 2 and 3.

D2: 0.6's clause 'which is now 128 (measured 2026-11-24: [Q#127] stands at 17-tools.md:50 and this line still read 127) - akiendelllinux_cc_0.' becomes 'which `cairn outlinecheck --next-qnum` prints - akiendelllinux_cc_0.', present tense with no dated aside (0.10.1; open-873bb5a20adb). The why of the change is this ticket's measured. The bracket goes: joined.markers read it as Q#127's marker in 0.6, and outlinecheck opened open-4f53f113cd1b, open-794c40aef083 and open-de5830d07fce on it, all answered as that false read.

D3: run() in outline_check.py answers argv ['--next-qnum'] by printing next_qnum(commons(root)/'questions'). next_qnum keeps 0.6's stated count as a floor when one is written (741d's scratch tooth holds that), so no mint logic changes. Code never writes the outline: open-37c55f5fcd67 (outline 0.10 / 0.9) refused the first D3, which had number_open rewrite 0.6's digits.

D4: 741d's test_every_live_open_question_has_a_number_and_its_marker_or_a_flag stops asserting 0.6 names a count and every marker is below it; it asserts 0.6 names cairn outlinecheck --next-qnum and every marker is below next_qnum. The count it bounded no longer exists; the decision is open-37c55f5fcd67's answer, bound to this ticket.

out: joined.py (its _STANDS grouping is b3472c7ee794's design and stands)

measured.saw: 47 Q# numbers on more than one record, 240 records, all resolved, each reading its number from the question text; Q#126 cited at 09-codemother-device.md:267 and [Q#127] at 17-tools.md:50 with no record; 0.6 reads 'now 128' while number_open minted up to Q#135
measured.how: joined.qnum over cairn.tools.question.question._all() and grep Q#12[6-9] over the requirements, house at ec53dff12

measured.saw: cairn outlinecheck b03dce633aa8 opened open-4f53f113cd1b: section 0.6 holds a [Q#127 bracket in its own by-line, so Q#127 reads as standing in two sections
measured.how: cairn outlinecheck b03dce633aa8, record outline_checks/b03dce633aa8-20261124T183357.json; grep -n Q#127 over the requirements

measured.saw: by identity alone (an 'outline: Q#n' note or an opening 'Q#n (' / 'Q#n:') no Q# is carried by two records: 0 duplicates. All 47 'duplicates' were outline_check's own records ('Ticket X touches section S, where Q#n stands open'), which joined.qnum's _STANDS reading files under the marker they cite, by design since b3472c7ee794. 110 numbers below 135 have no record, legal under outline 0.6.2 ('Questions live here and nowhere else... cairn question deprecated -amm'). So the cast's clauses 1 and 2 were dropped; the hypothesis 'bump 0.6 unless a bump cannot stay true' resolved to 'the mint keeps it': 741d's bump to 128 was stale within the same day
measured.how: identity-only qnum over cairn.tools.question.question._all(); git log -S_STANDS joined.py; sed -n 54,70p 00-how-to-read-this.md
